sets.relationshipLabel: opening and closing moment of one span
sets.explanation: Each pair marks the start and end of a natural cycle — day gives way to night, and cold gives way to warmth.

sets.relationshipLabel: storm system and its defining structural feature
sets.explanation: The eye and the anvil are the signature structural parts that let you identify each storm type at a glance.

sets.relationshipLabel: atmospheric cause and the physical effect it necessarily produces
sets.explanation: A pressure difference always produces wind, just as lightning always produces the thunder that follows it.

sets.relationshipLabel: visible sign and the severe weather it announces
sets.explanation: Storm-watchers read a wall cloud or a green sky as a warning sign that a specific hazard is imminent.

glossary.definition: A low, sinking, rotating patch of cloud that hangs down from a bigger storm cloud.

definitions.definition: The moment the sun first climbs over the horizon and morning begins.
The moment the sun dips below the horizon and evening takes over.
When temperatures drop enough that water turns hard and solid as ice.
When ice or frozen ground softens and turns back to liquid as it warms up.
A huge, spinning tropical storm with fierce winds and heavy rain.
The calm, clear patch right in the center of a spinning storm.
A storm with dark clouds, rain, and booming, crackling energy overhead.
The flat, spread-out top of a big storm cloud, shaped like a blacksmith's tool.
The weight of the air pressing down around you, always shifting place to place.
Air on the move, rushing from one place to another.
A sudden, bright flash of electricity that jumps between clouds or down to the ground.
The loud rumbling boom you hear after a flash lights up the sky.
A low, sinking, rotating patch of cloud that hangs down from a bigger storm cloud.
A violent, spinning funnel of wind that reaches down from a storm to the ground.
An eerie greenish tint the sky can take on during a nasty, dangerous storm.
Hard little balls of ice that fall from a storm cloud instead of rain.
